A job in /etc/cron.d.

```hcl
step "example" {
  cron {
    command = "..."
    name = "..."
    schedule = "..."
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | Yes | Command to run. |
| `name` | string | Yes | File name in /etc/cron.d: letters, digits, - and _. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | "delete" (default) removes the job, "forget" leaves it. |
| `schedule` | string | Yes | Five cron fields, or a macro such as @daily. |
| `user` | string | No | User the job runs as. Defaults to root. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_cron.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the job on the host matches. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_cron` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.
